title: Fastener Mechanical Property Class Seed Dataset
verification_method: Cross-checked against two independent manufacturer/industry-association engineering data sources per record where noted; ISO/SAE primary standard text itself was not directly read (paywalled/proprietary) -- see per-record provenance for exact sourcing and residual verification gaps. UI eligibility rule: a record's presence in this dataset does not by itself make it eligible for the eventual public calculator -- only fields carrying status 'verified' or 'source_bound' (never 'pending_verification' or 'unavailable') may be exposed; see audit/fastener-load-strength/PHASE-2-SOURCING-DATASET.md for the exact ready/blocked list per record.
primary_sources: ISO 898-1 (mechanical properties of fasteners made of carbon steel and alloy steel -- Part 1: Bolts, screws and studs with specified property classes), cited by all corroborating sources below; standard text itself not directly read in this phase
SAE J429 (Mechanical and Material Requirements for Externally Threaded Fasteners), cited by all corroborating sources below; standard text itself not directly read in this phase
Fastenal Engineering Data Sheet, 'Mechanical Properties Per ISO 898-1 (Externally Threaded Fasteners)', Rev 3-6-09 -- directly read and quoted
Nordic Fastening Group technical reference page, 'Mechanical properties, screws and studs EN ISO 898-1:2013' -- directly read and quoted
Southwest Bolt, 'SAE J429 Technical Specifications' data sheet (2020) -- directly read and quoted
Boltport Fasteners LLP, SAE J429 specification page -- directly read and quoted
license_notes: No copyrighted standards text (ISO 898-1 or SAE J429 itself) is reproduced. All numeric values are interpreted engineering reference values transcribed from freely-published manufacturer/industry-association engineering data sheets that themselves cite the governing standard, consistent with BoltLab's existing standards-citation practice (see data/standards/*/standards.seed.json).

yield_strength.note: Not given as a distinct field by either corroborating source; ISO 898-1 property class 4.6 is typically expressed via proof stress and Rm only in the sources checked.
